name: Eliab
overview: Eliab was a male leader from the tribe of Zebulun during the Exodus, serving as the head of his tribe at the time of the census as recorded in Numbers 1:9. His role as a tribal leader highlights his position of responsibility among the Israelites during their wilderness journey. He is noted specifically for his leadership among the Zebulunites.
namesAndTitles: The name Eliab means 'G-d is my father' in Hebrew, reflecting a theologically rich personal name that acknowledges God's fatherly relationship. This proper name, recorded in Numbers 1:9, does not indicate it was given directly by God but carries significant spiritual meaning.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records that Eliab was the son of Helon, establishing a direct familial lineage within the tribe of Zebulun. Beyond this, no additional family relationships are detailed in the biblical text for this individual.
scriptureSignificance: Eliab's significance in the biblical narrative centers on his leadership role as the head of the tribe of Zebulun during the Exodus census, which reflects God's orderly arrangement of the Israelite community. His mention underscores the importance of faithful tribal leaders in God's plan for His people. While another Eliab, the oldest brother of David, is noted elsewhere for being rejected by God despite outward appearance, this Eliab's record focuses on faithful service during a key moment in Israel's history.
